newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs signs trade pact with rump Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Czechs signs trade pact with rump Yugoslavia.

text.p: The Czech Republic and rump Yugoslavia on Friday signed a trade agreement in a step toward normalising relations between the two countries, Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said.

Dlouhy told reporters after a signing ceremony the agreement should renew contacts cut off by the beginning of the civil war in the former Yugoslavia and ease the economic sanctions on Belgrade that followed.
"The Czech Republic and its companies have a great interest in returning to that interesting market," Dlouhy said.
He said many possibilities existed for Czech companies in the energy and transportation sectors.

Yugoslavia's Trade Minister Djordje Siradovic said he hoped the agreement would help bring more balance to trade between the two countries since the Czech currently runs "a significant surplus in the exchange of mutual goods."
Czech exports to Yugoslavia rose to $39.2 million in the first eight months of this year from $16.6 million for the whole of 1995, according to preliminary figures.
Imports from Yugoslavia, meanwhile, rose only slightly to $3.9 million from $0.3 million.
